text:
Vincent Trocheck's first season in Utah, his fourth NHL organization, is getting heavier by the week. With the Mammoth's injuries piling up, he played 26:36 in the overtime loss to St. Louis on Nov. 12, and his ice time over the last ten games is up more than three minutes a night. He's the kind of center coaches lean on when the lineup thins out.

The scoring hasn't followed. He has 10 points in 20 games and no goals in his last nine, on 2.6 expected goals (the quality of his chances) over that stretch, so the drought is more bad luck than bad play. He's shooting 8.8% against a talent range near 13%. The five-on-five picture is good: Utah has had 58.9% of the expected goals with him on the ice.

Evolving-Hockey had him facing the toughest competition of almost any forward last season, and flagged that his results ran ahead of his chances then. This year it's the reverse. Watch whether the goals come back while the minutes stay this high.
headline: Trocheck is carrying more in Utah
